paragraphs.text: It starts low and honest. Mind, fickle as you are, you still get praised — because you court the refuge of refuges, the worlds teacher, Ambika’s husband. I climbed past the stairs of all the lesser gods and reached Shiva’s feet — and I still have not quit the low ground. Strange, but true. So the only prayer is: show me Your road, and shutter all world-doings tight, while I am Your ever-risen servant.

Then praise and petition, rapid-fire. Four names cried out: Shiva, Shiva, Shambhu, Shankara. Dissolved in His foot-lotus seat, making even the world taste good — laughing at Viriñchi, office-smeared and unmastered. Nothing shows apart from His light-body, so He is always already won, though far by nature. His foot-sap tastes stale to some, fresh-poured to others — shining, whole-bodied, void of two. My mind glints like lightning at dawn; if it would only hold steadier, worship would be complete. Thing or unthing — is anything beyond this? As You are, be bare to me. Set walking on His own road, why do I walk so ordinarily, knowing nothing worthy of His feet? Some god of His blooms in their hearts; His story-cloud thunders and its birds sing long. Love grows fat on play in Him, till parting-grounds fruit a union-feast. His word, watered by strange sap, slips even into slant hearts, its errand ever fresh.

Then longing wins out, paradox and all. They win on whose faces the Shiva-din circles. The fierce world as good as done, mind-stain thinned to nothing — yet not one atom of knocking at His city door. Hungry for one gaze into His ever-blooming face-lotus heart: flash facing me, just a little. Why does this slave go the wrong road, forsaking her — thought of His undifference, the only glory? Never unfit for His serfdom, unless sipping undifference-wine forever. Folk truly do not see His body, dirtied by two-sight — yet shelter-tender, do You not hear my wail? Remember any sense-joy I ever asked for? No — give only body-beholding nectar, my one wish. Give it. Hundreds of fair omens rose when I stepped on His road — what more could I hunt? What a Shiva-night reigns where sun goes down with moon. Three worlds’ overlordship I count sapless without His foot-touch nectar. Tough, this self-bond, tied by You alone — scorning You first, it slackens not one jot. And God-king, worshipped by the great, still stands worshiper-shaped alone, flashing in seers’ bodies, ever.
